messages:
mia: Heads-up — preparing a staged rollout for model v2 (hosted catalog). Thinking microsteps + signal gates. Need quick input on percent schedule, hold windows, and safety guards.

ashok: What are you thinking for absolute traffic volumes per step? Also do we isolate by tenant slices or just global percent? Noisy tenants can wreck metrics.

ben: Early proposal (rough): 0.1% -> 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%. Hold times: 10m, 20m, 30m, 60m, 60m respectively. Abort conditions: 5xx > 0.5% absolute OR p95 latency +25% vs baseline. Add internal smoke cohort at the 0.1% step.

mia: +1 on smoke cohort. For the first tiny step 10m seems fine, but for 1% maybe 15m is enough. Also suggest auto-exclude of any tenant that shows >2x error spike so they won't poison the global metric.

elena: We should also run a small eval harness at each step — say 200 synthetic prompts that check correctness/semantic regression. If any quality metric drops >2% we should pause. Telemetry hooks need to be part of the rollout policy.

ashok: Agree. Also add resource guards: cap per-GPU token/s and reject if GPU saturation > 80% for >2 min. That prevents cascading tail-latency.

ben: Example rollout snippet (for console/infra) — keep it minimal so UI can render it and users can tweak:

```yaml
rollout:
  name: model-v2-canary
  slices:
    - name: safety-cohort
      pct: 0.05
      selectors: [internal, smoke-customers]
    - name: general
      pct: rest
  steps:
    - pct: 0.1
      hold_sec: 600
    - pct: 1
      hold_sec: 900
    - pct: 5
      hold_sec: 1800
    - pct: 20
      hold_sec: 3600
    - pct: 50
      hold_sec: 3600
  abort_conditions:
    - metric: error_rate
      op: '>'
      value: 0.005
      window_sec: 300
    - metric: latency_p95
      op: 'pct_increase >'
      value: 25
    - metric: eval_quality_delta
      op: '<'
      value_pct: -2
  resource_guards:
    - metric: gpu_util
      op: '>'
      value: 80
      duration_sec: 120
  tenant_exclusion:
    enabled: true
    threshold_multiplier: 2.0
```

mia: This is good. For the console UX we should expose: 1) a templated schedule (fast/normal/slow), 2) per-step editable hold, 3) visible active telemetry checks and last-run eval results, and 4) manual override button (force-next-step / abort) with audit log.

elena: Also surface expected cost delta per step in the UI (rough token burn estimate) so product teams can make tradeoffs.

ben: How do we want to handle A/B experiments vs canary? If a customer requests A/B with persistent user buckets we need a separate "cohort allocation" mode that pins users, and metrics plumbing must be able to slice by assignment. That'll affect how we compute p-values for quality checks.

ashok: Good point. Keep canary "stateless percent routing" by default. Expose an alternate mode: "pinned cohorts" for experiments. Instrumentation should tag requests with allocation_id so analytics can partition.

mia: Ops checklist before kickoff: 1) add eval set + automation, 2) wire alerts for abort_conditions, 3) add tenant-exclude filter, 4) deploy console template, 5) run dry-run traffic simulation. Can someone own the dry-run?

ben: I'll run the simulation and post results by EOD.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Scheduled canary dry-run job created: job/rollout-sim-1715555555, ETA 2h. :gear:

elena: thanks — once simulation passes, we should do an internal canary to internal and partner traffic first.

mia: agreed. assigning owners: ben (simulation + initial rollout), elena (eval hooks + quality thresholds), ashok (resource/tenant guard rules). I'll open a PR for the console template with the YAML above. :white_check_mark:
